intended_object: Given an R-linear map f : M₁ → S (where S is an R-algebra-like semiring acting on M through a scalar tower) and a vector x ∈ M, the R-linear map b ↦ f(b) • x. This is the standard rank-one-type map built from a functional and a vector. Inferred from the docstring.
explanation: The definition sends b to f b • x. Additivity follows from f.map_add and add_smul. R-linearity follows from map_smul and smul_assoc, which uses IsScalarTower R S M. This is exactly what the docstring describes. The setting is about as general as it can be: semirings, additive commutative monoids, and S any semiring that is an R-module and acts on M compatibly through the scalar tower. No commutativity or field hypothesis is needed, and none is assumed. The usual case S = R is covered as a special instance. This is the Mathlib declaration itself, so there is no other, more general counterpart.
